statement: Galicia (northwestern Iberia, modern Galicia/Spain and northern Portugal) was briefly a separate kingdom under García II, son of Ferdinand I of León-Castile, who divided his realm among his sons at death (1065). García received Galicia; he was deposed by his brothers Sancho II and Alfonso VI (1071) and imprisoned until his death (1090). Galicia's distinct Celtic cultural heritage — Galician-Portuguese language, different legal customs — gave it a persistent regional identity even after reabsorption into León. The County of Portugal, carved from Galicia in 1093, eventually became an independent kingdom (1139).
